messages:
jess_support: FYI customer (ACME) reporting intermittent 502/504s from their private deployment. ALB target group shows health checks failing. Root cause unclear — requesting triage.

anita_customer: Health goes 0/2 in target group. Error from app logs: "upstream connect error or disconnect/reset before headers". Pods respond 200 to /health locally. When ALB hits the target we see TLS handshake failures in Envoy: "tls: handshake failure / connection reset".

alex_infra: Quick checks: is the target group protocol HTTP or HTTPS? ALB vs NLB behaviour differs. Also confirm security groups and NACLs allow ALB -> target traffic on health port. Can you paste target group config + SGs + a sample `describe-target-health`?

jess_support: Target group is IP targets, protocol HTTPS, port 443, health check path /health, matcher 200. ALB is internal. Pasting trimmed `aws elbv2 describe-target-health` output:
```
{ Target: 10.0.12.45:443, State: unhealthy, Reason: TCP connection timeout }
{ Target: 10.0.12.46:443, State: unhealthy, Reason: TLS handshake error }
```

mike_oncall: From infra side: ALB will attempt an HTTPS handshake to the target if TG protocol=HTTPS. If the target cert's CN/SAN doesn't match the Host header ALB uses for health checks (often the target IP), handshake will fail. Two typical fixes: 1) make health checks HTTP (if TLS is terminated upstream) or 2) ensure the health check Host header matches cert name / add SAN. Also confirm SGs allow traffic from ALB's subnets.

anita_customer: We ran `curl -v https://10.0.12.45:443/health` from a bastion and got: "SSL connected, wrong version number" then reset. Envoy logs show SNI '10.0.12.45' and cert CN=api.acme.com. Not surprising. Not sure how ALB decides Host/SNI for health checks.

alex_infra: ALB health checks default Host header to the IP for IP targets. That means SNI and cert mismatch. Solutions: - switch target group health check to use a custom Host header that matches your cert (e.g., api.acme.com) using `--health-check-host`, or - change TG protocol to HTTP if ALB is terminating TLS and talking HTTP to targets, or - use NLB for TLS passthrough so SNI/passthrough works. If using k8s ingress there's an annotation: `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/healthcheck-host: api.acme.com`.

jess_support: Proposed triage steps for customer: 1) from bastion, `curl -vk https://<target-ip>:443/health -H 'Host: api.acme.com'` to confirm host header fix; 2) if that works, update ALB target group health-check host override (or ingress annotation) and re-run. Also verify SGs: ALB subnets -> target SG allow 443.

anita_customer: Did the curl with Host header: `curl -vk https://10.0.12.45:443/health -H 'Host: api.acme.com'` -> 200 OK. So host header was the issue. How do we set that in our ALB via Terraform/annotations?

alex_infra: In AWS CLI: `aws elbv2 modify-target-group --target-group-arn <arn> --health-check-host 'api.acme.com'`. For k8s ALB controller use annotation `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/healthcheck-host: api.acme.com` and ensure `alb.ingress.kubernetes.io/healthcheck-protocol: HTTPS`. If you switch to HTTP health checks, set protocol and port accordingly. Also document: ALB will present SNI=Host header during health checks if you set the host override.

mike_oncall: I'm going to apply a temporary annotation to the ingress to set the healthcheck-host and open a security-group rule to allow ALB subnets to reach target SG. Will monitor for 15–30m and report. Escalated to eng-oncall if it doesn't clear.

jess_support: Customer reports after change: target health -> 2/2 and 502s vanished. Confirmed curl to public endpoint ok. Closing the thread. Action items: update support KB for ALB health check vs cert SNI mismatch, add quick checklist (curl from bastion with Host header, check TG protocol, ingress annotation, SG rules). :white_check_mark:
